narrative.overview: BlueHouse should feel like a precisely typeset daily bulletin made interactive: quiet enough for routine checking, exact enough to trust, and structured around the rates people seek first.
keyCharacteristics: Warm light and low-glare dark canvases with one clear indigo interface accent.
Official and blue rates dominate; operational freshness remains compact.
Space Grotesk, tabular figures, and strong alignment carry the hierarchy.
Dividers and tonal shifts replace decorative shadows.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Indigo occupies less than 10% of the interface and never indicates whether a rate rose or fell.

rules.name: The Figure First Rule
rules.body: Currency values receive the strongest weight and always use tabular numerals; labels never compete with them.

rules.name: The Bulletin Rule
rules.body: If a section needs a shadow to separate it, its spacing or divider hierarchy is wrong.

dos: Do place official and blue rates before every alternative quote.
Do use tabular numerals and exactly two decimal places for every peso value.
Do preserve a clear reading order from freshness, to current rates, to history.
donts: Don't resemble a crypto trading terminal: no neon, ticker density, speculative language, or alarmist movement cues.
Don't create a generic admin-dashboard grid that gives every metric equal visual weight.
Don't use side-stripe borders, gradient text, glassmorphism, or nested cards.
